newsitem.title: USA: Colonial line shut due to power outage from storm.
newsitem.headline: Colonial line shut due to power outage from storm.

text.p: Colonial Pipeline said its Line Four pipeline carrying refined products from Greensboro, North Carolina north to the Baltimore area was shut by a power outage due to Tropical Storm Fran.
"We experienced problems at several locations in North Carolina. Line Four is completely shut," said Noel Griese, spokesman for Colonial Pipeline.
He estimated the pipeline would be restored around noon Friday, adding that the impact to deliveries was minimal as the line was shut for only a few hours.
"The line serves points north to Baltimore, but flows north of that have not been affected," Griese said, referring to Line Three, which carries refined products from Greensboro to New York Harbor.
Colonial's delivery terminals, Apex and Selma, running out of Greensboro, were also hit by power outages.
"We can't make local deliveries till we get power back," Griese said, adding he could not estimate when the stations would resume operations.

Colonial's product lines carry nearly two million barrels per day (bpd) of gasoline and distillates from Houston to Greenboro, N.C. and to Linden, N.J. near the New York Harbor delivery points for NYMEX heating oil and gasoline futures.
